newsitem.title: UK: NWE heat oil under arbitrage pressure, diesel firm.
newsitem.headline: NWE heat oil under arbitrage pressure, diesel firm.

text.p: Northern European heating oil came under some pressure on Tuesday from rising supply, including cargoes from the U.S., the Red Sea and the Mediterranean, but diesel premiums jumped on strong demand, traders said. IPE Oct gas oil, which expires on Thursday, fell 25 cents to $247.00 per tonne and Nov dropped 50 cents to $240.25.

German heating oil cargo premiums were steady at Nov +$11/12 cif Hamburg for October delivery, but demand into France was weak, and some traders were looking at moving supply from the Red Sea to take advantage of Europe's recent price spike.

"We are seeing if we can move a cargo in from the Red Sea, and we are looking into getting some tax relief," said a trader with a large European refiner. This potential supply, in addition to about 570,000 tonnes of U.S. product fixed to sail to Europe in October and oversupply in the Mediterranean, put some pressure on the heating oil sentiment.

But diesel saw no such weakness, because most of the U.S. cargoes do not meet European cetane requirements. Diesel offers rose by $4 to Nov +$30 cif Le Havre for Oct 20-30, and attracted a bid as high as +$27 cif La Pallice.
